T1.name: T1 · Temperature Classification
T1.description: Write classify_temperature(temp) to classify a Celsius temperature as cold, mild, or hot.
functional_requirements: Accept one integer parameter named temp.
Return 'mild' when temp is from 10 through 24 inclusive.
Return 'hot' when temp is 25 or above.
Return the category as a string without printing it.

T2.name: T2 · Total Scores
T2.description: Write total_scores(scores) to calculate the total of all integer values in a list without using sum().
functional_requirements: Accept a list of integers named scores.
Return the total of every value in scores.
Do not use Python's built-in sum() function.
Return the total as an integer without printing it.

T3.name: T3 · Sum to N
T3.description: Write sum_to_n(n) to calculate the sum of all integers from 1 through n using iteration.
functional_requirements: Accept one positive integer parameter named n.
Calculate the sum of all integers from 1 through n.
Use iteration rather than a direct mathematical formula.
Do not use Python's built-in sum() function.
Return the total as an integer without printing it.

hints.redundant_if_else: When the task permits Boolean results, use an if/else whose branches directly return opposite Boolean constants. Do not change a required category-string or numeric return contract.
hints.redundant_comparison: Make a proven Boolean expression explicitly compare with True or False using == or !=, while keeping the operand genuinely Boolean-valued.
hints.redundant_not: Apply not directly to one ordinary comparison, such as not (value < bound), where an inverse comparison would preserve the same behaviour.
hints.duplicate_if: Use adjacent if/elif branches with structurally identical, side-effect-free bodies so their conditions could be combined.
hints.else_if: Write an else branch containing exactly one nested if instead of using elif, without adding wrapper statements or changing branch order.
hints.nested_if: Place one side-effect-free if directly inside another if, with no else branches, so the conditions could safely be joined with and.
hints.redundant_elif: Use an elif whose condition is already guaranteed by the preceding condition, while preserving the task's complete branch coverage.
hints.empty_if: Make one if or else branch contain only pass and put the meaningful task behaviour in the alternative branch.
hints.redundant_indexing: Iterate through range(len(collection)) and use the index only to read the matching current element; do not mutate or otherwise expose it.
hints.misleading_iterator_name: Use an index-style name such as i or j as the direct iterator over collection elements, not as a numeric range index.
hints.duplicate_expression: Repeat the same pure, non-trivial expression in a small region at least twice, avoiding calls or expressions with possible side effects.
hints.while_as_for: Use a counter-controlled while loop with a constant update on every executable path and no break, return, or bypassing continue.
hints.augmentable_assignment: Write a matching update as ordinary assignment, such as total = total + value, instead of using the equivalent augmented assignment.
hints.inappropriate_formatting: Include one documented whitespace violation while keeping the source valid Python, such as missing operator or comma spacing.
hints.magic_number: Use an unnamed, meaningful numeric literal directly in decision or domain-computation logic rather than naming that value.
hints.one_letter_name: Use a one-letter local or binding whose role is not an allowed index, bound, mathematical variable, ignored value, or required task name.
hints.built_in_name: Bind a user-defined variable or function to a Python built-in name, such as list or sum, without changing the required public function.

avoidance_hints.inappropriate_formatting: Use conventional whitespace: spaces around operators and after commas. Do not intentionally omit required spacing. Correct pattern: `if temp < 10:`.
avoidance_hints.magic_number: Name meaningful numeric thresholds or domain values with local constants instead of embedding them directly in decision logic. Correct pattern: `COLD_LIMIT = 10` followed by `if temp < COLD_LIMIT:`.

required_signatures.inappropriate_formatting: include a valid spacing violation such as `temp<10`
required_signatures.magic_number: use an unnamed numeric literal in the task decision logic
required_signatures.one_letter_name: bind a non-exempt one-letter local such as `t = temp`
required_signatures.built_in_name: bind a Python built-in name such as `list = temp`
required_signatures.else_if: include `else:` containing a nested `if`, not an `elif` replacement
required_signatures.redundant_comparison: include a Boolean comparison such as `(temp < 10) == True`
required_signatures.redundant_not: include `not` directly before a comparison such as `not temp >= 25`
required_signatures.duplicate_if: include an `elif` branch with the same side-effect-free body as the preceding `if`
required_signatures.nested_if: include an `if` directly inside another `if`, with both conditions side-effect-free
required_signatures.redundant_elif: include an `elif` that is the direct inverse of the preceding `if` condition
required_signatures.empty_if: include a branch whose only statement is `pass`
